_meta.indication: Combination ICS/LABA indicated for long-term, once-daily maintenance treatment of airflow obstruction in COPD, including chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema, and to reduce exacerbations of COPD in patients with a history of exacerbations; NOT indicated for acute bronchospasm or asthma

pivotal_trials.design: 24-week, randomized, multicenter, placebo-controlled, double-blind, parallel-group trial evaluating FF/VI 50/25 and 100/25 mcg once daily vs FF 100 mcg, VI 25 mcg, and placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Patients >=40 years with a COPD diagnosis per ATS/ERS definition (FEV1/FVC <=0.70)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline in trough FEV1 and weighted mean FEV1 (0-4h)
pivotal_trials.n: Randomized 207 placebo, 206 FF 100, 205 VI 25, 206 FF/VI 50/25, 206 FF/VI 100/25
pivotal_trials.result: Both co-primary endpoints met vs placebo (p<0.001 for all FF/VI to placebo comparisons). Trial 2206 FF/VI 100/25, Day 169 trough FEV1 difference from placebo 0.115 L (p<0.001); weighted mean FEV1 (0-4h) difference from placebo 0.173 L (p<0.001)

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, multicenter trial randomizing 1:1:1:1 to FF/VI 50/25, 100/25, 200/25 mcg or VI 25 mcg once daily
pivotal_trials.population: COPD patients with a documented history of at least one COPD exacerbation within 12 months of screening
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Annual rate of moderate and severe exacerbations
pivotal_trials.result: FF/VI 100/25 LS mean annual rate 0.70 vs VI 25 (rate ratio 0.66; 34% reduction, 95% CI 19, 46); because the highest dose (FF/VI 200/25) failed vs VI in the hierarchical testing, the p<0.001 for FF/VI 100/25 is a nominal/descriptive p value only

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=3%): nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, headache, and oral candidiasis. In 6-month trials, nasopharyngitis 9% (FF/VI 100/25) vs 8% placebo and headache 7% vs 5% placebo. Increased incidence of pneumonia: in 12-month trials in 3,255 subjects, FF/VI 100/25 pneumonia 6% (51 of 806) vs vilanterol 3% (27 of 818)
target_moa: Fixed combination of fluticasone furoate, a synthetic corticosteroid with anti-inflammatory activity, and vilanterol, a long-acting beta2-adrenergic agonist (LABA) bronchodilator — two different classes of medication
modality: Small molecule (inhaled corticosteroid + long-acting beta2-agonist dry powder inhalation)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: ASTHMA-RELATED DEATH — LABA, such as vilanterol, increase the risk of asthma-related death; a placebo-controlled US trial with another LABA (salmeterol) showed an increase in asthma-related deaths, considered a class effect of all LABA

rems.type: FDA determined a REMS is not necessary for Breo Ellipta at the time of approval; the sponsor's proposed REMS consisting of a Medication Guide and communication plan was not required

advisory_committee.vote: Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) met April 17, 2013; voted in favor of approval for airflow obstruction in COPD (9 yes, 4 no, 0 abstain) and for reduction of COPD exacerbation (8 yes, 5 no, 0 abstain)

description.text: Expanded asthma maintenance indication to pediatric patients 5 to 17 years, adding a new 50/25 mcg dosage strength for ages 5 to 11 years

citations.quote:
- Expansion of indication for Breo Ellipta (fluticasone furoate and vilanterol) 100/25 mcg to include maintenance treatment of asthma for patients aged 12 to 17 years.
- Expansion of indication for Breo Ellipta (fluticasone furoate and vilanterol) to include maintenance treatment of asthma in patients 5 to 11 years, with the addition of a new dosage strength of 50/25 mcg.

summary.text: Standard-review 505(b)(1) NDA for a fixed-dose ICS/LABA combination (fluticasone furoate 100 mcg and vilanterol 25 mcg inhalation powder; vilanterol a new molecular entity) for COPD; approved first cycle effective May 10, 2013 after a Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee meeting on April 17, 2013, with no accelerated approval and no REMS required

citations.quote: The product Breo Ellipta (fluticasone furoate 100 mcg and vilanterol 25 mcg inhalation powder) includes a novel dry powder inhaler device, the Ellipta inhaler, which contains 2 separate double-foil blister strips inside.
Vilanterol is a new molecular entity that belongs to the class called long-acting beta-2 adrenergic agonists (LABAs).
A meeting of the Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) was held on April 17, 2013, to discuss this application.
